findings.claim: The corrected uncharged bootstrap accounting is still not single-valued: the design asserts one canonical uncharged administrative resource ledger with one ceiling, yet it lets migration and bootstrap each bind their own Working AIP, ledger-binding and model/tool-call ceiling, so two administrative ledgers or two ceilings can exist and per-AIP exhaustion is not reconciled against the canonical ledger before P15 passes.
findings.evidence_excerpt: the HUMAN decision binds the objective, exact allowed write paths/effects, prohibited product/network/install/activation effects, one canonical uncharged administrative resource ledger, its resource/model-call ceiling, stop conditions, verifier, independent reviewer and HUMAN acceptance owner.
findings.impact: If migration's administrative binding and the bootstrap binding are not mechanically required to name the same canonical ledger identity and one cumulative ceiling, administrative calls can be recorded against a second ledger or a second ceiling; bootstrap can report nominal slack under P15 while the true cumulative administrative work is unaccounted, which is an undeclared effect and the residual form of the run-010 hidden-charge finding.
findings.recommended_action: Require the migration and bootstrap HUMAN decision records, the P15 receipt and the WBS-build entry evidence to bind one identical canonical administrative ledger path/identity plus one cumulative ceiling and reconciliation rule over that single ledger, and make divergence NOT_READY/BOOTSTRAP_BLOCKED rather than a note.

findings.claim: The migration authorization decision cannot be re-verified at the charge boundary: P13/P14/P15 re-hash and re-check only wbs_authority, bootstrap_authority and acceptance_authority, and the ledger_lineage receipt checks migrated-base byte lineage but not the migration decision record's identity, scope or revocation, so bytes produced under a stale or out-of-scope migration decision could satisfy P3 and form the accepted base for the first charge.
findings.evidence_excerpt: This authority cannot be reused for a charge write. For the first post-migration charge, P3/P15 require the pre-charge source to equal the exact HUMAN-accepted migrated base bytes/hash/version.
findings.impact: A migration performed under a decision record whose scope has been revoked, whose source hash/version changed, or whose acceptance is ambiguous is not mechanically detected by any pre-charge predicate; its output could become the admitted base, so admission can report READY while the frozen mission ledger was mutated under an unauthorized migration projection.
findings.recommended_action: Add the migration decision record to the bundle authority receipts (record ID, raw-record sha256, actor, bound pre-migration hash/version, scope and revocation state) and have P14 re-hash and re-check it, with absence, drift or revocation producing NOT_READY.

findings.claim: The artifact cannot demonstrate its asserted cumulative closure: it records correction only after formal run-010 needs_revision and pins only a v9 predecessor hash, with no finding-by-finding disposition showing that run-004 through run-009 confirmed findings and earlier observations are located and corrected in these exact bytes.
findings.evidence_excerpt: **Review state:** Corrected after formal run-010 `needs_revision`; requires a new high-risk council run before WBS build
findings.impact: The objective's cumulative-closure requirement is not verifiable from the reviewed artifact alone because peer findings and external advice are omitted from this lane's context; the v10 bytes cover run-010's bootstrap-accounting contradiction but carry no traceable evidence for the remaining run-004 through run-009 findings, so corrected and still-open prior findings cannot be distinguished before WBS build.
findings.recommended_action: Add to the design a finding-by-finding disposition table (prior finding ID, source run, confirmed/refuted/dispositioned, correcting section/line in v10), or require the council packet to include the prior run-004 through run-010 reports with hashes, so cumulative closure is checkable against the pinned bytes.
